Key features: white cottony material in the pod cavity, discolored/brown seeds, some seeds with gray mold coating. Top candidates: White_Mold (white cottony seeds in pods), Phomopsis (cracked shriveled seeds with gray mold).

Let me check reference images for the top candidates.

The White Mold reference shows stem symptoms. The test image shows opened pods with white cottony material and discolored/shriveled seeds - Phomopsis and Anthracnose are strong candidates too. Let me check more references.

The Anthracnose reference shows dark black pod lesions. Purple_Seed_Stain shows purple-stained seeds. Neither matches. The test image shows opened pods with white cottony material filling the cavity and discolored seeds - strongly suggesting White Mold ("white cottony seeds in pods").

Let me verify with a few more references.

None of these leaf diseases match. The test image clearly shows opened soybean pods with white cottony material filling the pod cavity and multiple discolored/shriveled seeds. This precisely matches the White Mold description: "white cottony seeds in pods."

Key distinguishing features in test image:
- White fluffy/cottony material filling the pod interior
- Seeds discolored (brown/tan), some shriveled
- Multiple opened pods showing consistent white mold colonization
- Not purple staining (rules out Purple_Seed_Stain)
- Not gray cracked seeds alone (Phomopsis)
- Anthracnose fills pod cavity with mycelium too but typically shows dark acervuli

The white cottony pod filling is the hallmark of White Mold and matches perfectly.
